extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in comedy controversies, corporate PR, and business/news media
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and considerations for judging offensive jokes and how companies should or do respond to them, especially when the comedian is a brand voice. Focuses on timing, appropriateness, company consistency, market impact, and reputation risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual sensitivity / timing
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is no place for anything but compassion and concern during these difficult times."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate jokes in light of current events and recent tragedies; material about a fresh disaster is judged more harshly. The page uses Aflac's quoted standard to justify condemnation of tweeting about the tsunami in Japan immediately after the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness versus funniness
rubrics_metrics.description: The article states of the two example tweets: "They are neither funny nor appropriate."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess both whether a joke succeeds as humor and whether it is appropriate for the situation and audience; even if a joke were technically 'funny,' appropriateness can be decisive in public response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severity of offense relative to comedian's history
rubrics_metrics.description: Gottfried's jokes about Japan are described as "among the least offensive he's ever made" in a career "built almost entirely on deliberately causing offense."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging a specific joke, compare its offensiveness to the comedian's established persona and history; prior patterns of deliberate offense inform expectations and responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate consistency / hypocrisy in enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece labels Aflac's action "an act of hypocrisy" given it has long tolerated Gottfried's more offensive material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a company enforces content/behavior standards consistently across time and contexts, or selectively when its commercial interests are affected; selective enforcement invites criticism of hypocrisy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market exposure and business interests as drivers of response
rubrics_metrics.description: The article argues Aflac's decision is "more likely a cynical reaction to the fact that 75 percent of its business is in Japan."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how a company's market concentration and customer base influence disciplinary decisions: firms may act primarily to protect revenue or market relationships rather than on principle alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior tolerance of offensive material toward other groups
rubrics_metrics.description: The article lists that Gottfried targeted "Blacks, Jews, women, gays" on Twitter and has a history of extremely offensive bits, yet Aflac's 'compassion' appeared only after the earthquake hit its No. 1 market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess patterns of tolerance: if offensive behavior toward certain groups was tolerated previously, critics will question motives when action is later taken only in specific cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial action by the comedian (deletion and apology)
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece notes Gottfried "deleted" the tweets and "apologized," yet was still fired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take into account whether a subject removed offending content and issued an apology and whether those remedial steps affect the appropriateness or severity of the employer's response; the article implies apology may be insufficient when market/reputation risk is high.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand-association risk and economic considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: The article speculates Aflac may replace him because it has "several years of tape" and that the new voice "will be cheaper than Gottfried's."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate decisions through the lens of brand risk management and cost: companies weigh the reputational cost of an association, the availability of alternatives, and potential savings when severing ties with a talent.
